paragraphs: Here's what I hear in Amos 6, friend. The people Amos is talking to had comfort, music, wine and the finest oils, and none of it was the problem by itself. The problem was that they were at ease and secure (Amos 6:1) while they did not grieve over the ruin of Joseph (Amos 6:6). Comfort got so thick around them that they couldn't see anybody else's pain.

Then there's the pride. They said, 'Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?' (Amos 6:13) And the LORD says He abhors Jacob's pride (Amos 6:8). When we give ourselves the credit, we stop looking up. They had also turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood (Amos 6:12), and a heart that's busy admiring itself doesn't have room for that kind of care.

So what does it mean for you, baker? The warning is real: the LORD says they will go into exile as the first of the captives (Amos 6:7), the great house will be smashed to pieces (Amos 6:11), and a nation will oppress them (Amos 6:14). Check your heart when life gets cozy, and ask who around you is hurting and who really gave you what you have. I've been in the back of a junk drawer, and I know what it's like to need somebody to notice, so go notice somebody.
